text:
lia_support: heads-up — NovaRetail (dedicated) is seeing repeated 429s + p95 token latency spikes since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says their traffic is steady but pool keeps scaling up/down (they called it a "scale yo-yo"). They want timeline and a fix.

alex_k: on it. Any customer request IDs or example request timestamps?

lia_support: sent a small sample: request ids 9f7a, 9f7b showing 429s at 09:11 and 09:14. Attaching customer note: "we saw ~60s periods where tail latencies jump and then nodes drain".

jordan_sre: grabbing autoscaler logs now. preliminary: saw scale events at 09:11 -> +2 nodes, 09:12 -> -2 nodes, 09:13 -> +1 node. Pretty tight churn.

alex_k: can you paste the autoscaler reasons?

jordan_sre: sure, snippet from controller logs:

```
2026-03-16T09:11:03Z autoscaler.go:234 scale_to=6 reason="inflight_requests > scale_threshold"
2026-03-16T09:11:45Z autoscaler.go:234 scale_to=4 reason="avg_gpu_util < 25%"
2026-03-16T09:12:48Z autoscaler.go:234 scale_to=5 reason="queued_requests > burst_threshold"
```

jordan_sre: metric spikes look bursty — queue depth oscillates, GPU util lags behind because new nodes take ~20s to warm KV caches. That mismatch causes overshoot then scale-down.

maria_g: could be noisy neighbor too — NovaRetail's pool shares hosts with other tenants on that Dedicated cluster (we allow bin-packing). Any recent large jobs on the cluster?

alex_k: checked infra events: around 09:10 a scheduled batch job for partner X started on same cluster (gpu-batch-03), spiking PCIe usage and increasing io_wait on a subset of hosts. That likely pushed node-level util low but queue high.

ops_lead: if autoscaler uses short cooldown + immediate thresholds we get exactly this: rapid up then immediate down. What's current cooldown?

jordan_sre: cooldown config for this customer pool is 60s scaleDownCooldown and 45s scaleUpCooldown. thresholds: queue>10 -> scale up, avg_gpu_util<30% -> scale down. No hysteresis.

alex_k: proposed quick mitigations:
- increase scaleDownCooldown to 5m for NovaRetail pool
- add hysteresis: require avg_gpu_util <30% for 2 consecutive checks (30s interval) before scale-down
- temporarily pin min_replicas=4 for NovaRetail for 30m while we validate
- add per-tenant queue cap to avoid noisy neighbor bursts impacting others

lia_support: NovaRetail needs a response + ETA. Can we do pin now? They already escalated to CSM.

jordan_sre: I can patch the pool config now. Running: 
```
kubectl -n redwood-autoscaler apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: PoolConfig
metadata:
  name: nova-retail-dedicated
spec:
  minReplicas: 4
  scaleDownCooldownSeconds: 300
  scaleUpCooldownSeconds: 60
  scaleDownConsecutiveChecks: 2
EOF
```

jordan_sre: applied. Also throttled bin-packing on that cluster to reduce co-located batch jobs for 1h.

maria_g: will follow up with infra to move the batch job off noisy hosts; assigning ticket INF-7192.

lia_support: thanks. I'll tell NovaRetail we've pinned capacity to 4 and we're tuning cooldowns; asking to hold off heavy bursts while we monitor. Offering temporary credit — ops_lead, can you approve? :slightly_smiling_face:

ops_lead: approve 10% credit for the affected window. Lia, send templated note and log the credit in billing ticket BILL-4631.

alex_k: follow-ups:
- I'll update autoscaler tests to simulate cache warm latency and ensure hysteresis prevents flapping.
- Add metric-based alert to detect >3 scale events in 5m for same pool.
- Investigate whether KV warm algorithm can be parallelized to reduce warm latency.

lia_support: customer response: "appreciate rapid fix — will watch for improvements and report if persists."

jordan_sre: monitoring now. so far no further scale-down within 5m window; p95 latencies falling back. Will leave this thread open for 2 hours then close.

sre-bot: alert suppressed for nova-retail-dedicated for 30m due to planned config change (runbook: scale-churn-mitigation).

lia_support: adding postmortem notes and owners to ENG-SRE board. tagging @alex_k and @jordan_sre for follow-up actions. :white_check_mark:

alex_k: thanks everyone — assigning myself to the code fix PR and jordan to infra changes.

maria_g: quick note for the runbook: include noisy-neighbor checks (recent host-level batch jobs, IO wait spikes) as a standard triage step.

lia_support: closing loop with customer at 11:00 UTC unless they reopen.
